verdicts.note: Open seat between two first-time candidates. She has never held office [S1][S6] but frames 19 years of banking, mortgage and recording work plus a year of training and peer-office tours as preparation [S6], so +1 rather than +2.

Timely, accurate audits and transparent fiscal reporting after the licensing-contract loss [S1][S3][S6] point to the audit-and-restrain pole. It is office-administration evidence, and Joyce makes the same audit promise, so -1 is as far as it goes.

Direction holds: no elected experience ('Not yet') and a statement framing the run as everyday citizens stepping up [S1]. +2 (the maximal outsider case) overstates it. The seat is open and her opponent is also a first-time candidate, so there is no incumbent to be the renewal case against. Her own priority is an office 'that runs smoothly today and grows stronger every year' [S2][S5], which describes continuity rather than overhaul. Her dossier body also never quotes the 'everyday citizens' line (it appears only in _contest.md and the scoring notes), and S4 (Daily World Q&A) carries no outsider framing in the dossier, so the score rests on S1 alone. +1 at medium puts her level with Paull, as two first-time candidates.

Genuinely mixed, so 0 is right: clean, timely audits and integrity in budget reporting and accounts [S2][S4] (pole a), alongside dedicated staff for elections and licensing, cross-training and back-up capacity, and college internships [S2][S4][S5] (pole b).

One clear statement, 'It's time to get money out of politics' [S1], plus a self-described grassroots, community-funded campaign [S5]. +1 at medium fits a single statement with no concrete reform proposal.
